about: The wheels for a game starting around 1500. Edit freely: slice labels (plus an optional "short" one for the wheel itself; the full label shows when it lands), blurbs, weights (higher = more likely; 0 = never), number ranges, name parts. Reload the page to see changes; mistakes show an error saying where. Wheels are spun in the order listed here.
name: c. 1500

notes.about: Where the numbers come from. Not shown in the game; for whoever tunes the ranges.
notes.odds: Placeholder weights for now: every normal slice is 1. Rare pulls: Government and Ideology each have one dark "rare" slice with "chance": 0.015 (1.5% of the wheel). Landing on it spins its own wheel of 7 rare results. A nation gets at most "rareLimit" rare pulls (1): after one, the other wheel's rare slice is left off. So about 3% of nations get one. Culture and Religion are switched off ("off": true) but kept for later.
notes.land: Area in km². Hard max 535,000 km² (1.5 × Germany's 357,600 km²); bigger is never rolled. The smallest real states c. 1500 (Ragusa, Lucca, the Italian and German city-states) held a few hundred to a few thousand km², so the wheel starts at 2,000.
notes.density: People per km² c. 1500, after Colin McEvedy & Richard Jones, Atlas of World Population History (1978), and Angus Maddison's population tables: steppe, taiga and desert well under 1–2; Muscovy ~2–3; Poland-Lithuania ~5; Iberia ~13; England ~19; France ~27; the German lands ~30; Italy ~35; Japan ~40; the Low Countries, Lombardy and the Ganges valley ~40–60. Population = land × density, so a small land can never hold a huge population.
notes.wealth: Output (GDP) per person c. 1500 from Angus Maddison's estimates, The World Economy: Historical Statistics (2003), in 1990 international dollars: bare subsistence ~400, Africa and the Americas ~415, Eastern Europe ~500, Japan 500, India 550, China 600, Portugal 606, Spain 661, Germany 688, England 714, France 727, the Netherlands 761, Belgium 875, Italy 1,100. Converted to today's money ×2.4 (US consumer prices 1990 → 2024) and rounded. GDP = population × output per person.
notes.check: Sanity check: a vast (≈535,000 km²), dense (25–40/km²), comfortable-to-prosperous nation comes out at ~13–21M people and ~$25–45B, in line with France c. 1500 (~15M people, Maddison GDP 10.9B 1990$ ≈ $26B today) and Italy (~10.5M, ≈ $28B). A city-state that's empty and destitute is a few thousand people and a few million dollars. Run game.checkNumbers() in the browser console to see the spread.

chart.about: Every nation gets a dot on this chart, from the "chart" pushes of its results: [x, y], each -1..1 (null = no push). x: left = liberal, democratic, peaceful; right = nationalist, dictatorship. y: bottom = miserable, top = a good life. The dot is the average push on each axis times "spread", kept inside the chart. The bonus wheel's slices grow the nearer their "at" is to the dot; the golden chance grows toward the corners.

names.about: A nation's name is a title picked by its government ("Sultanate of {place}"), with a made-up place name in it, and sometimes a word from its ideology ("Holy …"). Each government lists the name styles it draws from ("styles": arabic, turkic… from "places"); if the culture wheel is switched on, the culture picks the style instead. Titles: for each government, lists by key, tried in this order: the "prefer" wheel's slice (theocracy: religion, if spun), the name style and its tags ("arabic", "islamic"), any other result's slice id or tag, then "default". Place names: a start, sometimes a middle, an end, and sometimes a prefix; "smooth": false glues the parts as they are. Modifiers: by ideology, patterns where {name} is the whole name and {place} just the place ("Kingdom of Greater X"); used "modifierChance" of the time, and skipped if the title already has the word.
